segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Good Morning. Youth Council. Caroline speaking.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Oh, hello, I’m interested in standing for election to the Youth Council, and I was told to give you a call.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: That’s good. Could you I have your name, please?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Yes, it’s Roger Brown.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Thank you. I’m Caroline, the Youth Council administrator. So do you know much about what the Council does, Roger?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: I’ve talked to Stephanie – I think she’s the chair of the Council.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: That’s right.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: And she told me a lot about it. How it’s a way for young people to discuss local issues, for example, and make suggestions to the town council. That’s what made me interested.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Fine. Well let me take down some of your details. First of all, how old are you? You know the Council is for young people aged from 13 to 18?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: I’ve just turned 18.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: And where do you live, Roger?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Well, that’s a bit complicated. At the moment I’m looking for a flat to rent here, so I’m in a hostel from Monday to Friday [[ ]] . I go back to my parents’ place at the weekend.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: OK, so where’s the best place to send you some information about the Council?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Oh, to my parent’s address, please. That’s 17, Buckleigh [[ ]] Street – B-U-C-K-L-E-I-G-H Street, Stamford, Lincolnshire, though you don’t really need the country.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Oh, I know Stamford – it’s a lovely town. And what’s the postcode?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: PE9 7QT [[ ]]

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Right, thank you. So are you working here, or are you a student?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: I started studying at the university a couple of weeks ago, and I’ve got a part-time job for a few hours a week.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: What do you do?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Well, I’ve done several different things. I’ve just finished a short-term contract as a courier, and now I’m working as a waiter [[ ]] in one of the big hotels.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Uhuh. That can’t leave you much time for studying!

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Oh, it’s not too bad. I manage to fit it all in.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: What are you studying?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: My ambition is to go into parliament eventually, so my major subject is politics [[ ]] . That’s partly why I think the Youth Council is important and want to be a part of it.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: And I suppose you’re also taking a minor subject, aren’t you? I know a lot of people study economics too.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: I chose history. To be honest, I’m not finding it as interesting as I expected!

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: OK, so with your studying and your part-time job, do you have time for any other interests or hobbies?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Well, I spend quite a lot of time cycling [[ ]] – both around town to get to university and to work, and also long-distance, from here to London, for instance.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: That’s pretty impressive! Anything else?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: For relaxation I’m also keen on the cinema [[ ]] – I used to go at least once a week, but I can’t manage to go so often now.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Right. Are you sure you’ll have enough time for the Youth Council?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Yes, I’ve worked out that I can afford to reduce my hours at work, and that will make the time.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: So is there any particular aspect of the Youth Council’s work that appeals to you, Roger?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Well, my sister is blind, so I’m particularly interested in working with disabled young people [[ ]] , to try and improve the quality of their lives.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: That’s great. Well, the best way to get involved is to be nominated by some people who you know.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Right. Can you tell me how to set about organising that?

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: You should talk to Jeffrey, our Elections Officer. I can arrange a meeting in the council office with him, if you like.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Yes, please.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: He’ll be here next Monday, if that suits you

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: That’s the 14th, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: I can manage late afternoon.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Would you like to suggest a time? He generally leaves around 5.30.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Well, would 4.30 be OK [[ ]] ? My last class finishes at 4, so I’d have plenty of time to get to your office.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Right, that’s fine. Oh, and could I have a phone number we can contact you on?

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Yes, my mobile number’s 07788 136711. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Thank you. Well, we’ll look forward to seeing you next week.

segments.speaker: ROGER
segments.en: Thanks very much. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: CAROLINE
segments.en: Bye.
